lab: Create a production-ready transparent game sprite atlas, one square sheet with EXACTLY 3 columns and 3 rows of equal cells. Each cell contains one isolated prop centered with 15% empty padding, no overlap, no labels, no grid lines. Art direction: polished hand-painted Japanese monster-collecting RPG anime background prop art, clean dark blue ink outlines, soft cel shading, warm ivory painted metal with teal panels and restrained red indicator lamps. Slight top-down three-quarter view matching a 2D Pokemon laboratory dungeon. Tangible objects, not UI symbols, not vector diagrams, not pixel art, no characters. Soft contact shadows contained inside cells. All props consistent perspective and light from upper left. Row1 left: a believable waist-high laboratory emergency breaker console with a large red physical lever, cables, small glass meter, Pokeball-inspired round center seam design. Row1 center: floor-mounted laser emitter assembly with chunky teal housing and glowing red glass lens aimed to the right. Row1 right: recessed circular floor gas vent with visible slats, yellow/black caution rim, a small violet vapor wisp. Row2 left: circular hazardous electrical floor plate with copper conductors, insulators, yellow lightning warning triangle, teal frame. Row2 center: a closed transparent-lid technical machine reward case holding a colorful CD-like disc, cream casing with red round latch, recognizable Pokemon TM-inspired object. Row2 right: a purple and pink Pokemon Potion-inspired spray bottle with pale nozzle and translucent fluid. Row3 left: a gold keycard with Pokeball-inspired insignia and a metal key ring. Row3 center: a sealed cream and teal laboratory supply crate with inset red round latch, sturdy outlined corners. Row3 right: a rounded glass specimen canister holding muted violet fluid, cream base and rim, teal metal support. All nine fill similar cell area; no floating neon halos, no text. Genuine transparent background.
techniques: One production game ability-icon sprite atlas, square, exactly 5 columns by 5 rows equal size, transparent background, no text, no grid borders. Each illustration centered entirely in its own cell with 15% padding, no cell overlap. Beautiful Japanese Pokemon-style cel-painted attack illustrations, bold dark ink contours, chunky recognizable silhouettes with 2-3 shaded colors, readable when tiny. NOT thin line diagrams, NOT arrows as icons, NOT UI wireframes. Each is a miniature vivid illustration of a physical elemental attack with clear material. Row 1: (1) a luminous pink psychic energy orb with two curved aura wisps; (2) dark violet shadow ball with black smoky rim; (3) three gold five-point shooting stars; (4) exactly three touching elemental spheres red flame yellow electricity blue ice; (5) three orange burning embers. Row 2: (1) pale blue snowflake and icy wind curl; (2) single thick yellow electric spark; (3) a vivid rainbow pink-purple psychic energy beam shooting diagonally; (4) three pointed purple venom needles with green venom droplets; (5) blue-violet dragon-head-shaped energy wave, clearly dragon silhouette. Row 3: (1) green leaf drawing luminous green life droplets inward; (2) splashing purple sludge bomb with thick drops; (3) curling blue water cannon jet with white foam; (4) long cyan ice beam ending in sharp ice crystals; (5) branching powerful golden thunderbolt. Row 4: (1) long orange-red flamethrower plume with bright cream core; (2) a large violet energy sphere bursting into two small shards; (3) white winged running boot; (4) sharp amber feline eye; (5) blue energy sphere bouncing off a metallic shield, curved motion trail. Row 5: (1) unfurled cream map with an open violet eye emblem; (2) pink psychic orb duplicate for general attack; (3) shiny gold key; (4) small purple healing spray bottle; (5) rainbow technical-machine CD disc. Keep first 21 icons all distinct. Clear watercolor-cel surface shading, consistent Pokemon item-menu artwork language. No letters, numbers, emblems with text, panel backgrounds, neon wireframe symbols, characters. Genuine alpha transparency.
